newsitem.title: USA: Humana to buy Physician Corp. in $400 million HMO deal.
newsitem.headline: Humana to buy Physician Corp. in $400 million HMO deal.

text.p: Humana Inc., the nation's sixth-largest for-profit health management organisation, said Tuesday it has a definitive agreement to buy Physician Corp. of America for about $400 million.

In a bid to establish itself as a national force in the rapidly consolidating HMO marketplace, Humana agreed to pay $7 a share for Physician, which has health maintenance organisations in Florida, Texas and Puerto Rico.
Humana, based in Louisville, Ky., said it also will assume about $130 million of Physician Corp.'s debt.

Humana shares rose to a new high of $24 for the year on the news, before ending up 37.5 cents at $23.625 on the New York Stock Exchange. Shares in Miami-based Physician Corp. rose 37.5 cents to $6.625 on Nasdaq.
"It is a fabulous bargain" for Humana, said Michael LeConey, a health care industry analyst at the National Securities Corp. brokerage in New York.

Once the leader of the U.S. managed health care industry, Humana saw its star fade in recent years after it moved into unprofitable areas. Under new President Gregory Wolf, appointed last September, the company is battling back.

Assisted by a new executive staff, Wolf has pushed through a tough cost-cutting plan and sold off money-losing operations. With the retrenchment complete, Humana finally was able to buy Physician, a deal that was rumoured for months.
"It's a natural fit geographically," said Pamela Menefee, health care analyst at Robinson-Humphrey in Atlanta.
"It does not make them a national player. I don't think we really have any true national players yet. But it makes them a fairly significant player," she said.
The Humana-Physician deal adds momentum to a quickening pace of mergers and acquisitions among HMOs. Recent high-priced marriages in the sector have included:
-- Insurance giant CIGNA Corp.'s bid in February to acquire Healthsource Inc for $1.7 billion.
-- Pacificare Health Systems Inc.'s completion in February of its $2.2-billion acquisition of FHP International Corp.
-- Foundation Health Corp.'s and Health Systems International Inc.'s October merger valued at $3 billion.

"We expect that the consolidation of the HMO industry will accelerate dramatically in the next two years, and that this will redefine the industry," said Robert Hoehn, health care industry analyst at Salomon Brothers in New York.
"By the end of 1998, we expect that there will be one-half the number of HMOs that there are today," Hoehn said.
The Physician acquisition will add 1.1 million members to Humana, which already has 4.8 million members, and boost its annual premium revenues to about $8 billion from $6.9 billion, the company said.

Humana said it expects the acquisition to add between 8 cents and 10 cents a share to its earnings in 1998. In its most recent full year, Humana earned $12 million, or 7 cents a share, but those results included a one-time charge of $200 million related to restructuring.

The news came almost three months after Sierra Health Services Inc., of Las Vegas said it terminated a merger agreement with Physician Corp. That deal fell apart after Physician said it would take significant additional charges in the 1996 fourth quarter to cover increased liabilities at its workers' compensation unit.

Physician put itself on the block in early 1996. Rumours have circulated since then that Humana might be interested in buying it. Wall Street had originally pegged the purchase price near $24 a share in a stock transaction.
Since January 1996, Physician's stock price has fallen into the $4 to $7 range from a range of $15 to $18.
